miniProject.title: Native run-duration histogram with a strict pybind11 binding and a sanitizer-backed repair
miniProject.brief: Move one piece of taskrunner's reporting, the run-duration histogram, into C++ behind a strict Python boundary. Build it with CMake in debug, release and sanitizer trees, test it against NumPy as an oracle, document its layout and ABI, and follow a seeded memory error from the sanitizer report to a regression test.
steps: Write the core as a library function histogram(std::span<const double> x, double lo, double hi, std::span<std::int64_t> bins) that rejects lo >= hi or zero bins with std::invalid_argument, skips NaN and out-of-range values, and puts a value equal to hi in the last bin. Add an owning Histogram class with a deep copy, a move that leaves the source empty and bin access that throws std::out_of_range, and test copy independence, both moves and self-assignment in a native test executable.

Seed the defect: drop the clamp so a value equal to hi computes index n. In a clang++ 21.1 tree built with -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer, the input {0.0, 0.5, 1.0} over [0, 1] with four bins reports heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 8, 0 bytes after the 32-byte bins region, with the source line of the increment. Keep that input as a regression test expecting {1, 0, 1, 1}, restore the clamp, and on a repaired -O0 -g build use gdb (break histogram, run, bt, step to the index and print it) to connect the report to the frame.

Use numpy.histogram as the oracle. The plain index (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * n agrees with it on random values, but values on or next to a bin edge expose a difference: with values at each np.linspace edge and its two neighbors over 20,000 random non-dyadic ranges, it disagreed with NumPy 2.5.4 in 18,420. NumPy re-checks each index against its computed edges, k * ((hi - lo) / n) + lo with the last edge exactly hi. Port that check (step down when v is below the lower edge, up when it reaches the next edge and is not in the last bin) for 0 disagreements, or document and test your own edge rule.

Bind it with pybind11 3.1: take py::array_t<double, py::array::c_style> with .noconvert(), reject ndim != 1 and a data pointer not aligned to alignof(double) with ValueError, let pybind11 turn std::invalid_argument into ValueError, release the GIL only around the core call, and return a new int64 array owned by Python. Test that float32 input, a list, a[::2] and a[::-1] raise TypeError, that a 2-D array and an unaligned float64 view over a byte buffer at offset 1 raise ValueError, and that the result survives deletion of the input.

Build with CMake 4.2: the core library, the native tests registered with add_test, and the extension through pybind11_add_module, in build-debug, build-release and a clang++ build-asan tree that adds the sanitizer flags to compiling and linking. Run the sanitizer tree on the native tests, not on the extension inside an unsanitized Python. A deliberately false check must fail CTest in Debug and Release, and cmake --install must not install the tests.

Document the boundary: nm output for the core object and the extension (the exported PyInit_ symbol beside mangled C++ symbols), the extension suffix and the libraries ldd lists for it. Diagnose one failure from its message: an undefined reference when the tests link without the core library, or a core built as a shared library and run without it on the loader path, which exits 127 with error while loading shared libraries: ... cannot open shared object file while ldd shows not found.

Document layout and locality. For struct RunRecord { std::uint8_t status; std::uint64_t duration_us; std::uint32_t worker; }, g++ 15.2 on Linux x86-64 gives offsets 0, 8 and 16, size 24 and alignment 8; ordering the fields largest first gives offsets 0, 8 and 12 and size 16. Sum duration_us over a vector<RunRecord> and over a separate vector<std::uint64_t>, 1,048,576 records of i % 100 with both checksums 51,903,600, at -O2 with one warm-up and seven alternating timed scans per layout. Report raw times and medians, and keep cache explanations as hypotheses.

Split one histogram call across two std::thread workers that fill private bins and merge after join, and check the total equals the in-range count. Compare it with shared std::atomic<std::int64_t> bins incremented with relaxed fetch_add, and state why join makes the final read safe in both.
deliverables: The native component: core library, owning Histogram, native tests, the extension module and the CMake project with debug, release and sanitizer trees.
The sanitizer write-up: the seeded defect, the preserved ASan report, the gdb session and the regression that fails on the seeded code.
Binding tests for every accepted and rejected input and for output lifetime, and the NumPy oracle test with edge values.
A boundary note: symbols, extension suffix and linked libraries, the diagnosed link or loader failure, the RunRecord layout and the two-layout timing table.

rubric.pass: The binding agrees with numpy.histogram on random data and on values at and beside every edge, or a documented edge rule is tested instead.
rubric.strong: Edge cases come from a generator (Hypothesis or a seeded one), and the plain-index version is kept as a comparison that fails.

rubric.pass: Wrong dtype, a list, strided, reversed, 2-D and unaligned inputs are rejected with the stated exception types, and the result outlives the input.
rubric.strong: The binding names the owner of every buffer and the GIL state at each point, and says what would break if the GIL were released before the views were taken.

rubric.pass: The ASan report is preserved and explained line by line, and the regression fails on the seeded code in the sanitizer tree and passes after the repair.
rubric.strong: The write-up names what ASan and UBSan cannot prove here, such as a wrong but in-bounds bin.

rubric.pass: Debug, release and sanitizer trees build from scratch, CTest catches the false check in Debug and Release, and one link or loader failure is diagnosed from its message.
rubric.strong: The note says which upgrades (Python, compiler, NumPy) force a rebuild of the extension and why.

rubric.pass: Predicted offsets match the printed ones, both checksums are 51,903,600, and raw times are kept.
rubric.strong: The report separates the measured difference from cache explanations it did not test.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone native and diagnosis: the Python-native histogram, its sanitizer-backed repair and the gdb-backed write-up that becomes the evidence-first debugging report.
